title: French-Style Vanilla Custard Ice Cream
summary: A rich custard of cream, milk and egg yolks, gently cooked, chilled overnight and churned into smooth, scoopable vanilla ice cream.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Warm the dairy
steps.text: Put the cream, milk, half the sugar, the salt and the vanilla in the saucepan. Heat over medium heat, stirring, until steaming and the sugar has dissolved, about 5 min.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.text: In the heatproof bowl whisk the yolks with the remaining sugar until pale and slightly thickened.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisking all the time, pour a ladle of the hot cream into the yolks, then a second ladle. Pour the warmed yolks back into the pan. Adding heat gradually stops the yolks from scrambling.

steps.title: Cook the custard
steps.text: Stir constantly over low heat, scraping the base and corners with the spatula, for 5-8 min until the custard coats the spatula and a line drawn through it holds. It should read 77-80 °C. Never let it boil.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Strain the custard into a clean bowl and set it in the iced water, stirring until cool. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 h, ideally overnight; a really cold base churns smoother.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn in the ice-cream maker for 20-30 min until it is thick and holds its shape like soft serve.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Scrape into the container, press baking paper onto the surface and freeze for at least 4 h until firm enough to scoop. Let it soften for 5-10 min before serving.

tips: A vanilla pod, split and scraped into the warm cream, gives the best flavour and visible seeds.
If the custard starts to look grainy, pour it straight into a cold bowl and whisk hard.
Use the leftover whites for meringues or an omelette.
storage: Keep frozen in a covered container for up to 2 weeks; after that it slowly picks up ice crystals.
